collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A traveler has been telling strange, wrong stories about Isola: tell the village's own story to the next visitors, or ignore it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Visitors from another island have arrived, and they think the villagers eat sand and worship coconuts. A traveler has been telling stories about Isola, it seems, and getting nearly everything wrong. (friend) thinks it is hilarious. (subject) does not. How should the village answer?

choices.label: Let the Visitors Think What They Like

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) and (friend) put together an evening of stories for the visitors: the real founding, the real songs, the real reason nobody eats the purple crabs. The visitors listen, astonished. One of them laughs so hard at the crab story (other.he/she) falls off (other.his/her) log. They leave knowing a great deal more.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) decides it is not worth the trouble. (friend), on the other hand, decides it is worth a joke, and spends the whole visit solemnly bowing to coconuts. The visitors leave more confused than ever. (subject) is not amused. Everyone else is.
